minutes.headline: Task force heard a first stormwater utility overview and moved to let the DPW director seek funds for consultant work.
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force welcomed new members, heard a Flat Hill Road resident describe years of flooding and ice, then heard the consultant's first overview of a possible stormwater utility: funding target, three fee structures, billing, credits and the MS4 permit. A motion to give the DPW director permission to seek funds for the consultant's work was moved and seconded, but the result is not captured. Next meeting was set for March 21.

attendees.role: select board representative to the task force

public_comment.topic: Showed photos and a map of stormwater and ice flowing from Flat Hill Road across her property and toward Page Street, with erosion and a bus-stop safety concern, after years of complaints to the town since 2002; asked what a homeowner can do.

votes.motion: Motion to give the DPW director permission to seek funds to support the consultant's work on the stormwater utility; seconded, voice vote called.
Motion to adjourn, seconded, all in favor.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater utility funding pool and residential fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Consultant described a preliminary annual funding pool and residential fee range comparable to similar towns, and urged aiming higher because of construction cost inflation.
The earlier annual goal was about half the current target; consultant said the same work now costs roughly double.

budget_items.topic: Illustrative spending split of a utility
budget_items.what_was_said: Example split of the annual pool into personnel, equipment payments, replacement of failing catch basins and pipe, and smaller upgrade projects.
Flat fee, equivalent residential unit and impervious-area billing were compared; the middle option was recommended.
Braintree and Chelmsford charge a single residential rate of about the same size per year; Chelmsford has ten tiers.
Members favored adding the fee to the property tax bill to avoid costly separate mailings.
Credits shift the revenue shortfall onto other ratepayers; the group leaned toward deferring credits until the utility is established.
EPA has fined non-compliant communities; consultant gave example fine sizes.
Smaller towns may earmark money for an outside vendor instead of buying equipment used a couple weeks a year.
Discussion of state/federal stormwater funding, asset management grants, 604b, 319 (with cash match) and MVP action grants.

budget_items.topic: Consultant scope of work and notice to proceed
budget_items.what_was_said: Consultant has a stormwater utility task in an existing scope and needs notice to proceed; the agreement already has funds appropriated.

decisions.decision: Consultant and DPW director will work together on an annual revenue target and draft alternatives using the equivalent residential unit approach.
Group leaned toward deferring stormwater credits until the utility is established.
Minutes approval moved to next week's agenda because no minutes were available.
High school rain garden removed from ongoing business; DPW plans to install it in June.
Next meeting set for March 21 at 7 pm at the DPW.

what_happened.line: The task force heard the consultant's first overview of a possible stormwater utility: a funding target, three fee structures, billing, credits and the MS4 permit.
A motion to let the DPW director seek funds for the consultant's work was moved and seconded; the voice vote result is not audible in the recording.
The consultant and DPW director will draft an annual revenue target and alternatives using the equivalent residential unit approach.
Members favored putting any fee on the property tax bill, and leaned toward deferring stormwater credits until a utility exists.
The next meeting was set for March 21 at 7 pm at the DPW; minutes approval moved to that agenda because none were available.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility would be a new recurring charge, and the group favored collecting it on the property tax bill, so any fee structure chosen would show up in a resident's bill.

The group leaned toward billing by equivalent residential unit and deferring credits, which would make who pays more depend on the structure chosen. Nothing was adopted at this meeting, and a town meeting or ballot path was discussed but not decided.
